findings.note: Starter change: the Rays are starting Nick Martinez in Game 1 against Jacob Misiorowski instead of their ace, Drew Rasmussen. Some previews and lines assumed Rasmussen would start. Martinez had a 2.38 ERA on the road and held the Brewers to two runs over six innings in March.

SportsLine's model preview, written when Rasmussen was still the expected starter, cites Over trends: Over 19-13-1 in Rasmussen starts and Over 18-13-3 in Rays games with a total under 7. It also projects multiple total bases for the Rays' top three hitters.

ESPN's preview expects elite run prevention from both teams and low-scoring, close games. It points to the Brewers' bullpen (best among playoff teams), the Rays' rotation, the Rays' low walk rate and the Rays' weak hitting against 98+ mph fastballs.

CBS says Misiorowski hasn't finished five innings in either playoff start (88 pitches in the NLDS, 94 in the NLCS). His fastball is getting fewer whiffs and more fouls, and Murphy says he's well past his innings limit.

MLB.com says he has 11 strikeouts in 8 1/3 postseason innings and hasn't gotten out of the fifth. Opponents have beaten him by fouling off pitches to run up his count, and he'll be facing Nick Martinez in Game 1.

VSiN says he had 21 whiffs across two playoff starts and his spin looks fine. It adds that the Rays rank only 11th in whiff rate against 97+ mph fastballs, while the Padres and Dodgers were top-10 offenses in that split, which favors him. VSiN leans Rays +162 and made no strikeout pick.

VSiN leans Rays moneyline at +162 but notes Martinez's 15.1% strikeout rate, a 3.97 xERA and a .309/.344/.470 line with a 5.15 ERA the third time through the order, which raises the risk of an early hook before 14 outs.
SportsLine's Game 1 preview confirms Martinez starts against Misiorowski, with Milwaukee at about -198, and says Martinez has a 6.10 ERA over his last five games against the Brewers.

ESPN confirms Martinez starts Game 1 on five days' rest after 5⅓ innings (16 outs) in ALCS Game 4; MLB.com says his two postseason starts total 9 innings, so the other was about 11 outs, which splits around the 13.5 line.

MLB.com's Game 1 preview (Oct 22): the Rays held back ace Rasmussen and are starting Nick Martinez against Misiorowski, who led MLB in ERA (1.80), Ks and WHIP. Milwaukee's bullpen has a 1.33 postseason ERA. The Rays are only missing McClanahan, and Woodruff is Milwaukee's open question.

CBS/SportsLine lists Brewers -198 / Rays +162, so the +165 offered is barely better than the market. Milwaukee went 59-26 at home and Martinez has a 6.10 ERA in his last five games vs MIL. The model's free pick is Over 6.5; its moneyline side is paywalled.

VSiN's analyst leans Rays +162 as a value play because the line looks too big. Reasons given: Misiorowski's high pitch counts this October and Martinez's sinker against Milwaukee's weakness on sinkers. The writer still expects the Brewers to win, and the Rays were only 43-38 on the road.
